- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; apply downward bias correction by 1–3% for 30d forecasts.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >70), model often overshoots in subsequent days; cap forecast growth to 0.5–1.0% per day post-spike.
- If official supply net is negative and bearish sentiment dominates, model underestimates downside risk; add 1–2% downward adjustment to forecast mean.
- When sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish mid-period, model fails to adjust; apply early mean reversion rule: reduce forecast slope by 0.1–0.3 per day after sentiment drop.
- For 30d forecasts with high event count and negative supply net, model tends to overreact to recent auctions; use 3-day moving average of true prices to smooth forecast baseline.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model exhibits lagged response; delay forecast adjustment by 1–2 days relative to sentiment shift.
